{"parentUuid":"569408ad-40aa-412a-9a36-c578d97fd46f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49744d0f-faa0-4995-b293-4e614a407edc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01P6fbPEBKBwkyYeQvoZpUPM","type":"tool_result","content":"{\"body\":\"## Parent\\n\\n#1 (Spec: Kenyon Model UN Recaps CMS)\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nAdmins create, edit, delete, Publish and Unpublish Pages. A Page has a title, a Slug, a text-only Markdown Body, a Draft or Published status and a nav position. Each Page records its Owner and when it was created and last edited. The Page editor has a Preview that uses the shared sanitizer. The Pages list can be filtered by status. A Page Slug is refused if it is reserved (`trips`, `images`, `admin` or `login`) or already used by another Page. Editing or Unpublishing a Published Page shows the \\\"still live until you Deploy\\\" notice. Editors are refused on every Page route.\\n\\nOn the Public site, each Published Page is written at `<page>/`. Every page carries a Navigation bar of Home first, then the Published Pages ordered by nav position.\\n\\nSettled: Pages are text-only and have no Images. Contact emails on an \\\"Officers and contact\\\" Page are plain text, and `mailto:` links are stripped like any other external link.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- [ ] An Admin can create, edit, delete, Publish and Unpublish a Page. Every Page starts as a Draft.\\n- [ ] Owner, created and edited timestamps are recorded.\\n- [ ] A reserved Slug (`trips`, `images`, `admin`, `login`) and a duplicate Page Slug are each refused with a clear error.\\n- [ ] The Pages list filters by status.\\n- [ ] Page Preview shows the sanitized Body, with external links, `mailto:` links, images and raw HTML removed.\\n- [ ] Editing or Unpublishing a Published Page shows the \\\"still live until you Deploy\\\" notice.\\n- [ ] Every Page route is added to the table-driven Editor test, and Editors get a 403 or a redirect on each one.\\n- [ ] `render_site` writes Published Pages and omits Draft Pages.\\n- [ ] Every page in the output has a Navigation bar listing Home, then the Published Pages in nav order, with relative links that resolve from every depth.\\n- [ ] No `href=\\\"/` or `src=\\\"/` appears anywhere in the output.\\n- [ ] Every Page form carries a CSRF token.\\n\\n## Blocked by\\n\\n- #5 (T04)\\n- #6 CMS)\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nAdmins create, edit, delete, Publish and Unpublish Pages. A Page has a title, a Slug, a text-only Markdown Body, a Draft or Published status and a nav position. Each Page records its Owner and when it was created and last edited. The Page editor has a Preview that uses the shared sanitizer. The Pages list can be filtered by status. A Page Slug is refused if it is reserved (`trips`, `images`, `admin` or `login`) or already used by another Page. Editing or Unpublishing a Published Page shows the \\\"still live until you Deploy\\\" notice. Editors are refused on every Page route.\\n\\nOn the Public site, each Published Page is written at `<page>/`. Every page carries a Navigation bar of Home first, then the Published Pages ordered by nav position.\\n\\nSettled: Pages are text-only and have no Images. Contact emails on an \\\"Officers and contact\\\" Page are plain text, and `mailto:` links are stripped like any other external link.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- [ ] An Admin can create, edit, delete, Publish and Unpublish a Page. Every Page starts as a Draft.\\n- [ ] Owner, created and edited timestamps are recorded.\\n- [ ] A reserved Slug (`trips`, `images`, `admin`, `login`) and a duplicate Page Slug are each refused with a clear error.\\n- [ ] The Pages list filters by status.\\n- [ ] Page Preview shows the sanitized Body, with external links, `mailto:` links, images and raw HTML removed.\\n- [ ] Editing or Unpublishing a Published Page shows the \\\"still live until you Deploy\\\" notice.\\n- [ ] Every Page route is added to the table-driven Editor test, and Editors get a 403 or a redirect on each one.\\n- [ ] `render_site` writes Published Pages and omits Draft Pages.\\n- [ ] Every page in the output has a Navigation bar listing Home, then the Published Pages in nav order, with relative links that resolve Decisions behind it: ADR-001 (local admin console, static Public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Editors write at the Sunday meetings; only Admins Publish).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon Model UN club has no website. Trip recaps go on Instagram, where they sink in the feed, so nobody in the Kenyon community can look back at a past Trip. The President and Vice President want a place where members' Recaps of each Trip (where the team went, how the competition went, what they explored and ate) are published with photos and stay findable. Members need to be able to write their own Recaps. The officers must stay in control of what reaches readers, and no member can ever change another member's work or touch accounts.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the **Console laptop**. Admins and Editors log in to it. Editors write their own Recaps at the Sunday club meetings and Submit them. Admins review, edit, Send back, or Publish them. Admins also manage Trips, Pages, and Accounts, and enter Recaps for Contributors who email their writing in.\n- A static **Public site** that an Admin Deploys from the terminal. It lists Trips newest first. Each Trip page shows its Summary and then its Published Recaps. Admin-written Pages, such as \"About the club\", form the Navigation bar. A footer link sends readers to Instagram for discussion. Only Published content reaches the Public site, and all of it is sanitized.\n\nAn Admin can also take a dated Backup of the database and Images with `cms backup`, so losing the laptop doesn't lose the club's writing.\n\n## User Stories\n\n**Login and Accounts**\n\n1. As an Admin, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use Admin powers on the Console laptop.\n2. As an Editor, I want to log in with my own Account at the Sunday meeting, so that my Recaps are mine and nobody else's.\n...\n</persisted-output>","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"b73ab238-f7fe-4a64-bb7d-143903d3a211","timestamp":"2026-10-24T17:03:32.394Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`. The President and Vice President want a place where members' Recaps of each Trip (where the team went, how the competition went, what they explored and ate) are published with photos and stay findable. Members need to be able to write their own Recaps. The officers must stay in control of what reaches readers, and no member can ever change another member's work or touch accounts.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the **Console laptop**. Admins and Editors log in to it. Editors write their own Recaps at the Sunday club meetings and Submit them. Admins review, edit, Send back, or Publish them. Admins also manage Trips, Pages, and Accounts, and enter Recaps for Contributors who email their writing in.\n- A static **Public site** that an Admin Deploys from the terminal. It lists Trips newest first. Each Trip page shows its Summary and then its Published Recaps. Admin-written Pages, such as \"About the club\", form the Navigation bar. A footer link sends readers to Instagram for discussion. Only Published content reaches the Public site, and all of it is sanitized.\n\nAn Admin can also take a dated Backup of the database and Images with `cms backup`, so losing the laptop doesn't lose the club's writing.\n\n## User Stories\n\n**Login and Accounts**\n\n1. As an Admin, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use Admin powers on the Console laptop.\n2. As an Editor, I want to log in with my own Account at the Sunday meeting, so that my Recaps are mine and nobody else's.\n3. As any logged-in person, I want to sign out, so that the next member at the laptop can't act as me.\n4. As an anonymous visitor to the console, I want to be redirected to the login page from every console page, so that nothing in the console is reachable without an Account.\n5. As an Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n6. As a person who typed a wrong password, I want a generic \"email or password is incorrect\" message, so that the login page doesn't reveal which emails have Accounts.\n7. As an Admin, I want a Deactivated Account to be unable to log in, and any session it already has to stop working, so that a member who leaves the club loses access immediately.\n\n**Roles and permissions**\n\n8. As an Admin, I want Editors to get a 403 or a redirect on every Admin-only page and action, so that the Editor role is genuinely limited.\n9. As an Editor, I want to create Recaps, edit and delete my own Drafts, add Images to them, and Submit them, so that I can contribute without waiting on an officer.\n10. As an Admin, I want an Editor to be unable to Publish or Unpublish anything, so that Published always means an Admin approved it.\n11. As an Editor, I want to be refused when I try to view, edit, Submit, or delete another person's Recap, so that nobody can tamper with my writing.\n12. As an Editor, I want my Recap locked against my own edits once it is Submitted or Published, so that what an Admin reviewed doesn't change underneath them.\n13. As an Admin, I want to do everything an Editor can, and also edit or delete any Recap, so that I can fix typos and take down anything inappropriate.\n\n**Trips**\n\n14. As an Admin, I want to create a Trip with a conference name, host city, start date, end date, and Summary, so that Recaps have something to belong to.\n15. As an Admin, I want the Trip's Slug suggested from its year and city (such as `2026-chicago`) and editable, so that addresses are readable.\n16. As an Admin, I want to edit any Trip, so that I can correct its Summary or dates later.\n17. As an Admin, I want deleting a Trip refused while it still has Recaps, so that Recaps are never lost along with their Trip.\n18. As an Editor, I want to pick the Trip my Recap is about from a list, so that I can't misspell or invent a Trip.\n\n**Recaps**\n\n19. As an Editor, I want to write a Recap with a title, a Slug, and a Markdown Body, so that I can tell my story with basic formatting.\n20. As an Editor, I want the Slug suggested from the title, so that I don't have to think about URLs.\n21. As an Admin, I want a Recap's Slug to be unique within its Trip, with a clear error on a clash, so that two Recaps never share an address.\n22. As an Editor, I want my Byline (name and class year) filled in from my Account, so that I'm credited correctly without typing it.\n23. As an Admin entering a Contributor's emailed Recap, I want to type their name and class year as the Byline, so that the Contributor is credited and not me.\n24. As an Admin, I want every Recap to record its Owner and when it was created, last edited, and Published, so that I know who is responsible for it and how fresh it is.\n25. As an Admin, I want saving or Submitting a Recap with no Body text to be refused, so that no Recap is just photos.\n26. As an Editor, I want to Submit my finished Draft, so that the Admins know it's ready to review.\n27. As an Admin, I want to Send back a Submitted Recap to Draft, so that its Editor can revise it.\n28. As an Admin, I want to Publish a Draft or Submitted Recap, so that it goes out with the next Deploy.\n29. As an Admin, I want to Unpublish a Published Recap back to Draft, so that I can take it down at the next Deploy.\n30. As an Admin editing or Unpublishing a Published Recap or Page, I want a notice that the change is \"still live until you Deploy\", so that I don't assume readers already see the change.\n31. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Recap while it is a Draft, so that I can abandon a false start.\n\n**Images**\n\n32. As an Editor, I want to upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo of up to about 5 MB to my Recap, with required alt text, so that my Recap has pictures that screen readers can describe.\n33. As an Editor, I want the console to give me a ready-to-paste Markdown snippet with my alt text filled in after an upload, so that I can place the photo where I want it in my Body.\n34. As an Admin, I want uploads of any other file type, or larger files, refused with a clear message, so that the Public site doesn't fill up with huge or unsafe files.\n35. As an Admin, I want Publish refused while the Body has an image without alt text, so that the Public site stays accessible.\n36. As an Admin, I want a Recap's Images deleted along with the Recap, so that orphaned photos don't pile up.\n\n**Pages and Navigation bar**\n\n37. As an Admin, I want to create, edit, and delete Pages (title, Slug, text-only Markdown Body, Draft or Published), so that the club has an \"About\" page and an \"Officers and contact\" page.\n38. As an Admin, I want each Page to record its Owner and when it was created and last edited, so that Pages are accountable like Recaps.\n39. As an Admin, I want to set a number for each Page's position in the Navigation bar, so that I control the order of the links.\n40. As an Admin, I want a Page Slug refused if it is reserved (`trips`, `images`, `admin`, `login`) or already used by another Page, so that addresses never collide.\n41. As an Editor, I want the Pages area to be closed to me, so that the role boundary is obvious.\n\n**Admin console**\n\n42. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of Recaps by status (Draft, Submitted, Published), Trips, Pages by status, and active Accounts, so that I can see at a glance what needs attention.\n43. As an Editor, I want my dashboard to show counts of my own Recaps by status, so that I know what I still owe.\n44. As an Admin, I want a \"changes not yet live\" notice on the dashboard whenever content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so that I remember to Deploy.\n45. As an Admin, I want a content list of Recaps that I can filter by status, by Trip, and by Owner, with Submitted Recaps shown first, so that I can find what to review quickly.\n46. As an Editor, I want the content list to show only my own Recaps, filterable by status and Trip, so that I see my own work and nobody else's.\n47. As an Admin, I want a Pages list I can filter by status, so that I can find Drafts.\n48. As an Editor or Admin, I want a Preview button on the Recap and Page editor that reloads the page showing the sanitized, rendered Body exactly as readers will see it, so that I can check formatting and Image placement before saving or Submitting.\n49. As any console user, I want every form to carry a CSRF token, and any submission without a valid one refused, so that another website can't make my browser act for me.\n\n**Account management (Admin only)**\n\n50. As an Admin, I want to create an Account with an email, name, class year, role, and initial password, so that the members the President and VP chose can log in.\n51. As an Admin, I want to change an Account's role between Editor and Admin, so that officer changes can be handled.\n52. As an Admin, I want to Deactivate an Account while its Recaps, Pages, and Bylines stay, so that departing members lose access without their writing disappearing.\n53. As an Admin, I want Deactivating or demoting the last active Admin refused, so that the club can never lock itself out.\n54. As outgoing officers at Handover, we want to create the incoming Admins' Accounts and have them Deactivate ours, so that control transfers cleanly each year.\n\n**Public site and Deploy**\n\n55. As a Kenyon reader, I want the home page to list Trips newest first, so that I see the latest Trip immediately and can scroll back to older ones.\n56. As a reader, I want each Trip's page to show its Summary and then its Published Recaps in the order they were Published, with their Bylines, so that I get the overview and then each member's story.\n57. As a reader, I want a Trip to appear only once it has at least one Published Recap, so that I never land on an empty Trip.\n58. As a reader, I want a Navigation bar with Home first, then the Published Pages in the order the Admins set, so that \"About the club\" is always one click away.\n59. As a reader, I want a footer link to the club's Instagram for discussion, so that I can react to a Recap even though the site has no comments.\n60. As an Admin, I want `cms publish` to write only Published Recaps and Pages, and only Trips that have a Published Recap, into `site/`, so that Drafts and Submitted Recaps never leak.\n61. As an Admin, I want every Body sanitized when it is rendered, with scripts and raw HTML stripped and external links and external images removed, so that nothing harmful or off-site reaches readers.\n62. As an Admin, I want every link and image in `site/` to be a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n63. As an Admin, I want only the Images of Published Recaps copied into `site/`, so that photos from Drafts never become public.\n64. As an Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push `site/` live, so that a Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`.\n\n**Backup and seed data**\n\n65. As an Admin, I want `cms backup` to write one dated archive containing the database and all uploaded Images to a folder I choose outside the repository, so that I can keep a private copy on the club's Drive.\n66. As an Admin, I want `cms backup` to refuse to write inside the repository, so that a Backup can never be committed by accident.\n67. As a grader, I want the seed script to create one Admin and one Editor (passwords from the environment), a Trip, Recaps in each status, and a Draft and a Published Page, so that I can try every capability on a fresh clone.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Storage.** SQLite through the standard library, at the existing database path setting. The schema:\n\n- **Account**: email (unique, used to log in), name, class year, role (`admin` or `editor`), argon2 password hash, active flag, created timestamp.\n- **Trip**: conference name, host city, start date, end date, Summary, Slug (unique), created and edited timestamps.\n- **Recap**: Trip, Owner (an Account), title, Slug (unique per Trip), Body (Markdown), Byline name, Byline class year, status (`draft`, `submitted`, `published`), and created, edited, and Published timestamps.\n- **Page**: Owner, title, Slug (unique), Body (Markdown), status (`draft`, `published`), nav position, and created and edited timestamps.\n- **Image**: Recap, stored file name, original type, size, alt text.\n- **Site state**: a single record holding when `cms publish` last ran, which the \"changes not yet live\" notice uses.\n\n**Byline.** The Byline is copied onto the Recap when it is created: from the Owner's Account, or typed by an Admin for a Contributor. Admins can edit it. Renaming or Deactivating an Account later doesn't rewrite existing Bylines.\n\n**Recap status machine.** Every Recap starts as a Draft.\n\n| From | To | Who |\n|---|---|---|\n| Draft | Submitted | the Editor who Owns it |\n| Submitted | Draft (Send back) | Admin |\n| Draft or Submitted | Published | Admin |\n| Published | Draft (Unpublish) | Admin |\n\nEditors may edit or delete only their own Drafts. Admins may edit or delete any Recap. Pages go between Draft and Published, and only Admins move them.\n\n**Permission policy.** A single module answers \"can this Account do this action to this object\". Every route asks it, so there are no ad-hoc role checks scattered across routes. Being logged out redirects to login. Being logged in but not allowed returns 403. The policy rereads the Account on every request, so a Deactivation or role change takes effect at once.\n\n**Login and sessions.** Login takes an email and password at `/login`, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. Sessions use a signed cookie through the existing `itsdangerous` dependency. Sign out clears the session. Login failures show one generic message.\n\n**CSRF.** Each session has a token, rendered as a hidden field in every form that changes state. Any state-changing request without a matching token gets a 403. No new dependency.\n\n**Markdown rendering.** One function turns a Body into HTML: `markdown-it-py`, then `nh3` with an allowlist of formatting tags. It removes:\n- any link whose target is not relative,\n- any image whose source is not one of the Recap's own uploaded Images,\n- all raw HTML.\n\nPreview and `cms publish` both use this same function, so what Preview shows is what readers get.\n\n**Images.** Accepted types are JPEG, PNG, and WebP, checked by file content and not by extension, up to about 5 MB. Images are stored in an uploads folder that is gitignored and outside `site/`. The snippet the console offers is a relative `images/<file>` reference. `cms publish` copies a Published Recap's Images next to its page, so that relative reference resolves.\n\n**Admin console screens.**\n- Login.\n- Dashboard, with counts and the \"changes not yet live\" notice.\n- Recaps list with filters for status, Trip, and Owner (Owner for Admins only), Submitted first for Admins.\n- Recap editor with Preview, Image upload, and action buttons for the transitions above.\n- Trips list and editor.\n- Pages list (filter by status) and editor with Preview and nav position.\n- Accounts list and editor.\n\nAll console routes sit under `/admin`, except `/login` and `/logout`. Screens are server-rendered with Jinja. There is no JavaScript framework and no live preview (ADR-002).\n\n**Admin-only routes.** These must refuse Editors:\n- Trip create, edit, and delete.\n- All Page routes.\n- All Account routes.\n- Publish, Unpublish, and Send back.\n- Editing, Submitting, or deleting a Recap the Editor doesn't Own.\n\n**Public site rendering.** `render_site` writes:\n- the home page (Trips with a Published Recap, newest start date first),\n- one page per such Trip,\n- one page per Published Recap,\n- one page per Published Page,\n- the stylesheet,\n- copied Images.\n\nAddresses take the forms `trips/<trip>/`, `trips/<trip>/<recap>/` and `<page>/`, each as an index file. Every link is computed relative to the page's depth. The Navigation bar is Home followed by the Published Pages by nav position. The footer holds the Instagram link, taken from a constant committed in the repository's settings (not an environment variable), so `cms publish` produces the same footer on any machine with no setup. Its value is the placeholder `https://www.instagram.com/REPLACE-ME/` for now. Nothing that isn't Published is ever read by the renderer.\n\n**Deploy and Backup run from the terminal only.** Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`, both of which already exist. The console has no Deploy or Backup button. \"Only Admins Deploy and Backup\" holds because the terminal belongs to the President.\n\n**`cms backup`.** A new subcommand on the existing CLI. It takes the SQLite online-backup copy of the database and the uploads folder, and zips them with the standard library into `cms-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.zip` in an output folder given as an argument. It refuses any output folder inside the repository. Backup archives are also gitignored as a second safeguard.\n\n**Seed data.** Extend the existing seed script. Its Admin and Editor emails match the test fixture, and passwords come from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. It creates demo content in every status.\n\n**`CONTEXT.md`.** The Deploy entry now says that a Deploy is `cms publish` (render) plus `cms deploy` (push). It is corrected in the same commit that references this spec.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test drives the system from outside and checks what a user or reader would see: HTTP status codes, redirects, page text, and files written to `site/`. Tests don't reach into tables or private functions. They use only the seams that already exist, and no new seams are added.\n\n**Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Tests use `TestClient` with the `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. The fixtures may be extended so each test gets a temporary database with the demo Accounts seeded. That changes how the fixtures are set up, not which seam the tests use. The required tests are:\n\n- **Anonymous visitors**: requesting every console route redirects to login.\n- **Editors on Admin-only routes**: a table-driven test hits every Admin-only route and action listed above as an Editor and expects a 403 or a redirect for each one.\n- **Editors cannot Publish**: an Editor's Publish and Unpublish requests are refused, and the Recap's status stays the same.\n- **Editors cannot touch another person's Recap**: edit, Submit, and delete requests on someone else's Recap are refused, and the Recap is unchanged.\n- **Editors are locked out after Submit**: an Editor can't edit their own Recap once it is Submitted or Published.\n- **Passwords**: the stored password is an argon2 hash and never the plain text. Logging in with the right password works, and with a wrong one fails with the generic message. Signing out ends the session.\n- **Deactivation**: a Deactivated Account can't log in, and its existing session stops working. Deactivating or demoting the last active Admin is refused.\n- **Role changes**: after an Admin changes an Account's role, its permissions follow the new role.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form contains a token, and a POST without a valid token gets a 403.\n- **Recap rules**: Submit, Send back, Publish, and Unpublish each move the status as specified. An empty Body is refused. A Slug that clashes within its Trip is refused. Deleting a Trip that has Recaps is refused.\n- **Image rules**: wrong file types, oversized files, and missing alt text are refused. Publish is refused while the Body has an image without alt text.\n- **Dashboard**: the counts match the seeded data, for both an Admin and an Editor.\n- **Content list**: the status, Trip, and Owner filters return the right Recaps. Editors see only their own Recaps.\n- **Preview**: given a Body containing `<script>`, an external link, and an external image, Preview shows sanitized HTML with all three removed.\n\n**Seam 2: `render_site(out)` into `tmp_path`.** These tests follow the prior art in `tests/test_t00.py`. Using a seeded database, they check:\n\n- Draft and Submitted Recaps, Draft Pages, and Trips with no Published Recap are absent from the output.\n- Published content is present.\n- Body sanitization holds in the output.\n- The Navigation bar lists Home, then the Published Pages in nav order.\n- No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` appears anywhere.\n- Only the Images of Published Recaps are copied.\n\n**Existing CLI entry point: `main(argv)`.** `cms backup` writes a dated archive containing the database and the uploads, and refuses an output folder inside the repository.\n\nThe tests in `tests/test_t00.py` must keep passing.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments on the Public site. This is a known gap, and the Instagram footer link stands in for it.\n- Images on Pages, as a possible later addition. Pages are text-only.\n- A hosted or remote admin console. Editors use the Console laptop (ADR-001, ADR-003).\n- Deploy and Backup buttons in the console.\n- Reactivating a Deactivated Account. Admins create a new Account instead (see Further Notes).\n- A live preview, a WYSIWYG editor, drag-and-drop, multi-site, tags and categories, and search.\n- Password reset by email. An Admin sets a new password instead.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n**Coverage of the seven required capabilities**\n\n| # | Capability | Where this spec covers it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Login: sign in and out, hashed passwords | Stories 1–7. Login, sessions and argon2 decisions. Password and Deactivation tests. |\n| 2 | Two roles with genuinely different permissions | Stories 8–13 and 41. Permission policy. Admin-only route list. Required 403-or-redirect and Recap-ownership tests. |\n| 3 | Posts (here, Recaps and Trips): CRUD, title, Slug, Markdown Body, draft and published, author, timestamps | Stories 14–31. Schema (Owner as author, Byline as the displayed author). Status machine. |\n| 4 | Pages, with published Pages in the nav | Stories 37–41 and 58. Page schema. Navigation bar rendering. |\n| 5 | Admin console: dashboard counts, filterable content list, editor with Preview | Stories 42–49. Console screens. Dashboard, content list and Preview tests. |\n| 6 | User management: Admin-only, create, change role, Deactivate, Deactivated users can't log in | Stories 50–54. Account schema and policy. Deactivation and role tests. |\n| 7 | Public site and publish: only published content, sanitized Markdown, nav from Pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths | Stories 55–64. Rendering and sanitizer decisions. Seam 2 tests. |\n\n**Reactivation.** Reactivating a Deactivated Account never came up while the design was settled. This spec leaves it out to keep the Account rules small. Raise it before ticketing if the officers want it.\n\n**Instagram handle.** The footer link is a placeholder, `https://www.instagram.com/REPLACE-ME/`. The owner will replace it with the club's real Instagram handle before the final publish.\n\n**Who can Deploy.** \"Only Admins Deploy and Backup\" is enforced by the Console laptop's terminal being the President's, not by code. This is a deliberate trade-off, made in the spec session.\n\n\n----\n     100 app/db.py\n     142 app/recaps.py\n      10 app/templating.py\n     127 app/accounts.py\n      61 app/security.py\n \"/admin/probe-one\", \"/admin/probe-two\"):\n        r = c.get(path, follow_redirects=False)\n        assert r.status_code == 303 and r.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\", path\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/login\", \"/logout\"])\ndef test_anonymous_post_without_a_token_is_refused(client, path):\n    # fresh client: no session cookie at all, so there is no token to match\n    r = client.post(path, data={\"email\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n                                \"password\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"]},\n                    follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code == 403\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_default_secret_key_logs_a_warning(database, monkeypatch, caplog):\n    from app import settings\n    from app.main import create_app\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SECRET_KEY_IS_DEV_DEFAULT\", True)\n    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):\n        create_app()\n    assert \"CMS_SECRET_KEY is not set\" in caplog.text\n11:- An **admin console** that runs only on the **Console laptop**. Admins and Editors log in to it. Editors write their own Recaps at the Sunday club meetings and Submit them. Admins review, edit, Send back, or Publish them. Admins also manage Trips, Pages, and Accounts, and enter Recaps for Contributors who email their writing in.\n12:- A static **Public site** that an Admin Deploys from the terminal. It lists Trips newest first. Each Trip page shows its Summary and then its Published Recaps. Admin-written Pages, such as \"About the club\", form the Navigation bar. A footer link sends readers to Instagram for discussion. Only Published content reaches the Public site, and all of it is sanitized.\n23:4. As an anonymous visitor to the console, I want to be redirected to the login page from every console page, so that nothing in the console is reachable without an Account.\n25:6. As a person who typed a wrong password, I want a generic \"email or password is incorrect\" message, so that the login page doesn't reveal which emails have Accounts.\n30:8. As an Admin, I want Editors to get a 403 or a redirect on every Admin-only page and action, so that the Editor role is genuinely limited.\n40:15. As an Admin, I want the Trip's Slug suggested from its year and city (such as `2026-chicago`) and editable, so that addresses are readable.\n47:19. As an Editor, I want to write a Recap with a title, a Slug, and a Markdown Body, so that I can tell my story with basic formatting.\n48:20. As an Editor, I want the Slug suggested from the title, so that I don't have to think about URLs.\n49:21. As an Admin, I want a Recap's Slug to be unique within its Trip, with a clear error on a clash, so that two Recaps never share an address.\n58:30. As an Admin editing or Unpublishing a Published Recap or Page, I want a notice that the change is \"still live until you Deploy\", so that I don't assume readers already see the change.\n69:**Pages and Navigation bar**\n71:37. As an Admin, I want to create, edit, and delete Pages (title, Slug, text-only Markdown Body, Draft or Published), so that the club has an \"About\" page and an \"Officers and contact\" page.\n72:38. As an Admin, I want each Page to record its Owner and when it was created and last edited, so that Pages are accountable like Recaps.\n73:39. As an Admin, I want to set a number for each Page's position in the Navigation bar, so that I control the order of the links.\n74:40. As an Admin, I want a Page Slug refused if it is reserved (`trips`, `images`, `admin`, `login`) or already used by another Page, so that addresses never collide.\n75:41. As an Editor, I want the Pages area to be closed to me, so that the role boundary is obvious.\n79:42. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of Recaps by status (Draft, Submitted, Published), Trips, Pages by status, and active Accounts, so that I can see at a glance what needs attention.\n81:44. As an Admin, I want a \"changes not yet live\" notice on the dashboard whenever content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so that I remember to Deploy.\n84:47. As an Admin, I want a Pages list I can filter by status, so that I can find Drafts.\n85:48. As an Editor or Admin, I want a Preview button on the Recap and Page editor that reloads the page showing the sanitized, rendered Body exactly as readers will see it, so that I can check formatting and Image placement before saving or Submitting.\n92:52. As an Admin, I want to Deactivate an Account while its Recaps, Pages, and Bylines stay, so that departing members lose access without their writing disappearing.\n98:55. As a Kenyon reader, I want the home page to list Trips newest first, so that I see the latest Trip immediately and can scroll back to older ones.\n99:56. As a reader, I want each Trip's page to show its Summary and then its Published Recaps in the order they were Published, with their Bylines, so that I get the overview and then each member's story.\n101:58. As a reader, I want a Navigation bar with Home first, then the Published Pages in the order the Admins set, so that \"About the club\" is always one click away.\n103:60. As an Admin, I want `cms publish` to write only Published Recaps and Pages, and only Trips that have a Published Recap, into `site/`, so that Drafts and Submitted Recaps never leak.\n105:62. As an Admin, I want every link and image in `site/` to be a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n107:64. As an Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push `site/` live, so that a Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`.\n113:67. As a grader, I want the seed script to create one Admin and one Editor (passwords from the environment), a Trip, Recaps in each status, and a Draft and a Published Page, so that I can try every capability on a fresh clone.\n120:- **Trip**: conference name, host city, start date, end date, Summary, Slug (unique), created and edited timestamps.\n121:- **Recap**: Trip, Owner (an Account), title, Slug (unique per Trip), Body (Markdown), Byline name, Byline class year, status (`draft`, `submitted`, `published`), and created, edited, and Published timestamps.\n122:- **Page**: Owner, title, Slug (unique), Body (Markdown), status (`draft`, `published`), nav position, and created and edited timestamps.\n124:- **Site state**: a single record holding when `cms publish` last ran, which the \"changes not yet live\" notice uses.\n137:Editors may edit or delete only their own Drafts. Admins may edit or delete any Recap. Pages go between Draft and Published, and only Admins move them.\n152:**Images.** Accepted types are JPEG, PNG, and WebP, checked by file content and not by extension, up to about 5 MB. Images are stored in an uploads folder that is gitignored and outside `site/`. The snippet the console offers is a relative `images/<file>` reference. `cms publish` copies a Published Recap's Images next to its page, so that relative reference resolves.\n156:- Dashboard, with counts and the \"changes not yet live\" notice.\n160:- Pages list (filter by status) and editor with Preview and nav position.\n163:All console routes sit under `/admin`, except `/login` and `/logout`. Screens are server-rendered with Jinja. There is no JavaScript framework and no live preview (ADR-002).\n167:- All Page routes.\n173:- the home page (Trips with a Published Recap, newest start date first),\n174:- one page per such Trip,\n175:- one page per Published Recap,\n176:- one page per Published Page,\n180:Addresses take the forms `trips/<trip>/`, `trips/<trip>/<recap>/` and `<page>/`, each as an index file. Every link is computed relative to the page's depth. The Navigation bar is Home followed by the Published Pages by nav position. The footer holds the Instagram link, taken from a constant committed in the repository's settings (not an environment variable), so `cms publish` produces the same footer on any machine with no setup. Its value is the placeholder `https://www.instagram.com/REPLACE-ME/` for now. Nothing that isn't Published is ever read by the renderer.\n192:A good test drives the system from outside and checks what a user or reader would see: HTTP status codes, redirects, page text, and files written to `site/`. Tests don't reach into tables or private functions. They use only the seams that already exist, and no new seams are added.\n205:- **Recap rules**: Submit, Send back, Publish, and Unpublish each move the status as specified. An empty Body is refused. A Slug that clashes within its Trip is refused. Deleting a Trip that has Recaps is refused.\n213:- Draft and Submitted Recaps, Draft Pages, and Trips with no Published Recap are absent from the output.\n216:- The Navigation bar lists Home, then the Published Pages in nav order.\n227:- Images on Pages, as a possible later addition. Pages are text-only.\n231:- A live preview, a WYSIWYG editor, drag-and-drop, multi-site, tags and categories, and search.\n242:| 3 | Posts (here, Recaps and Trips): CRUD, title, Slug, Markdown Body, draft and published, author, timestamps | Stories 14–31. Schema (Owner as author, Byline as the displayed author). Status machine. |\n243:| 4 | Pages, with published Pages in the nav | Stories 37–41 and 58. Page schema. Navigation bar rendering. |\n246:| 7 | Public site and publish: only published content, sanitized Markdown, nav from Pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths | Stories 55–64. Rendering and sanitizer decisions. Renaming or Deactivating an Account later doesn't rewrite existing Bylines.\n\n**Recap status machine.** Every Recap starts as a Draft.\n\n| From | To | Who |\n|---|---|---|\n| Draft | Submitted | the Editor who Owns it |\n| Submitted | Draft (Send back) | Admin |\n| Draft or Submitted | Published | Admin |\n| Published | Draft (Unpublish) | Admin |\n\nEditors may edit or delete only their own Drafts. Every route asks it, so there are no ad-hoc role checks scattered across routes. Being logged out redirects to login. Being logged in but not allowed returns 403. The policy rereads the Account on every request, so a Deactivation or role change takes effect at once.\n\n**Login and sessions.** Login takes an email and password at `/login`, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. Sessions use a signed cookie through the existing `itsdangerous` dependency. Sign out clears the session. Login failures show one generic message.\n\n**CSRF.** Each session has a token, rendered as a hidden field in every form that changes state. Any state-changing request without a matching token gets a 403. No new dependency.\n\n**Markdown rendering.** One function turns a Body into HTML: `markdown-it-py`, then `nh3` with an allowlist of formatting tags. It removes:\n- any link whose target is not relative,\n- any image whose source is not one of the Recap's own uploaded Images,\n- all raw HTML.\n\nPreview and `cms publish` both use this same function, so what Preview shows is what readers get.\n\n**Images.** Accepted types are JPEG, PNG, and WebP, checked by file content and not by extension, up to about 5 MB. Images are stored in an uploads folder that is gitignored and outside `site/`. The snippet the console offers is a relative `images/<file>` reference. `cms publish` copies a Published Recap's Images next to its page, so that relative reference resolves.\n\n**Admin console screens.**\n- Login.\n- Dashboard, with counts and the \"changes not yet live\" notice.\n- Recaps list with filters for status, Trip, and Owner (Owner for Admins only), Submitted first for Admins.\n- Recap editor with Preview, Image upload, and action buttons for the transitions above.\n- Trips list and editor.\n- Pages list (filter by status) and editor with Preview and nav position.\n- Accounts list and editor.\n\nAll console routes sit under `/admin`, except `/login` and `/logout`. Screens are server-rendered with Jinja. There is no JavaScript framework and no live preview (ADR-002).\n\n**Admin-only routes.** These must refuse Editors:\n- Trip create, edit, and delete.\n- All Page routes.\n- All Account routes.\n- Publish, Unpublish, and Send back.\n- Editing, Submitting, or deleting a Recap the Editor doesn't Own.\n\n**Public site rendering.** `render_site` writes:\n- the home page (Trips with a Published Recap, newest start date first),\n- one page per such Trip,\n- one page per Published Recap,\n- one page per Published Page,\n- the stylesheet,\n- copied Images.\n\nAddresses take the forms `trips/<trip>/`, `trips/<trip>/<recap>/` and `<page>/`, each as an index file. Every link is computed relative to the page's depth. The Navigation bar is Home followed by the Published Pages by nav position. The footer holds the Instagram link, taken from a constant committed in the repository's settings (not an environment variable), so `cms publish` produces the same footer on any machine with no setup. Its value is the placeholder `https://www.instagram.com/REPLACE-ME/` for now. Nothing that isn't Published is ever read by the renderer.\n\n**Deploy and Backup run from the terminal only.** Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`, both of which already exist. The console has no Deploy or Backup button. \"Only Admins Deploy and Backup\" holds because the terminal belongs to the President.\n\n**`cms backup`.** A new subcommand on the existing CLI. It takes the SQLite online-backup copy of the database and the uploads folder, and zips them with the standard library into `cms-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.zip` in an output folder given as an argument. It refuses any output folder inside the repository. Backup archives are also gitignored as a second safeguard.\n\n**Seed data.** Extend the existing seed script. Its Admin and Editor emails match the test fixture, and passwords come from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. It creates demo content in every status.\n\n**`CONTEXT.md`.** The Deploy entry now says that a Deploy is `cms publish` (render) plus `cms deploy` (push). It is corrected in the same commit that references this spec.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test drives the system from outside and checks what a user or reader would see: HTTP status codes, redirects, page text, and files written to `site/`. Tests don't reach into tables or private functions. They use only the seams that already exist, and no new seams are added.\n\n**Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Tests use `TestClient` with the `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. The fixtures may be extended so each test gets a temporary database with the demo Accounts seeded. That changes how the fixtures are set up, not which seam the tests use. The required tests are:\n\n- **Anonymous visitors**: requesting every console route redirects to login.\n- **Editors on Admin-only routes**: a table-driven test hits every Admin-only route and action listed above as an Editor and expects a 403 or a redirect for each one.\n- **Editors cannot Publish**: an Editor's Publish and Unpublish requests are refused, and the Recap's status stays the same.\n- **Editors cannot touch another person's Recap**: edit, Submit, and delete requests on someone else's Recap are refused, and the Recap is unchanged.\n- **Editors are locked out after Submit**: an Editor can't edit their own Recap once it is Submitted or Published.\n- **Passwords**: the stored password is an argon2 hash and never the plain text. Logging in with the right password works, and with a wrong one fails with the generic message. Signing out ends the session.\n- **Deactivation**: a Deactivated Account can't log in, and its existing session stops working. Deactivating or demoting the last active Admin is refused.\n- **Role changes**: after an Admin changes an Account's role, its permissions follow the new role.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form contains a token, and a POST without a valid token gets a 403.\n- **Recap rules**: Submit, Send back, Publish, and Unpublish each move the status as specified. An empty Body is refused. A Slug that clashes within its Trip is refused. Deleting a Trip that has Recaps is refused.\n- **Image rules**: wrong file types, oversized files, and missing alt text are refused. Publish is refused while the Body has an image without alt text.\n- **Dashboard**: the counts match the seeded data, for both an Admin and an Editor.\n- **Content list**: the status, Trip, and Owner filters return the right Recaps. Editors see only their own Recaps.\n- **Preview**: given a Body containing `<script>`, an external link, and an external image, Preview shows sanitized HTML with all three removed.\n\n**Seam 2: `render_site(out)` into `tmp_path`.** These tests follow the prior art in `tests/test_t00.py`. Using a seeded database, they check:\n\n- Draft and Submitted Recaps, Draft Pages, and Trips with no Published Recap are absent from the output.\n- Published content is present.\n- Body sanitization holds in the output.\n- The Navigation bar lists Home, then the Published Pages in nav order.\n- No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` appears anywhere.\n- Only the Images of Published Recaps are copied.\n\n**Existing CLI entry point: `main(argv)`.** `cms backup` writes a dated archive containing the database and the uploads, and refuses an output folder inside the repository.\n\nThe tests in `tests/test_t00.py` must keep passing.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments on the Public site. This is a known gap, and the Instagram footer link stands in for it.\n- Images on Pages, as a possible later addition. Pages are text-only.\n- A hosted or remote admin console. Editors use the Console laptop (ADR-001, ADR-003).\n- Deploy and Backup buttons in the console.\n- Reactivating a Deactivated Account. Admins create a new Account instead (see Further Notes).\n- A live preview, a WYSIWYG editor, drag-and-drop, multi-site, tags and categories, and search.\n- Password reset by email. An Admin sets a new password instead.\n=== app/db.py\n\"\"\"SQLite access. The database path is read from settings on every call.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS account (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    name          TEXT NOT NULL,\n    class_year    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trip (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    conference TEXT NOT NULL,\n    city       TEXT NOT NULL,\n    start_date TEXT NOT NULL,\n    end_date   TEXT NOT NULL,\n    summary    TEXT NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')),\n    edited_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recap (\n    id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    trip_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES trip (id),\n    owner_id          INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES account (id),\n    title             TEXT NOT NULL,\n    slug              TEXT NOT NULL,\n    body              TEXT NOT NULL,\n    byline_name       TEXT NOT NULL,\n    byline_class_year INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    status            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'\n                      CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'submitted', 'published')),\n    created_at        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')),\n    edited_at         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')),\n    published_at      TEXT,\n    UNIQUE (trip_id, slug)\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS image (\n    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    recap_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES recap (id),\n    filename     TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    content_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n    size         INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    alt          TEXT NOT NULL,\n    created_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS site_state (\n    id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),\n    last_rendered_at  TEXT\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open a connection; commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        yield conn\n        conn.commit()\n    except BaseException:\n        conn.rollback()\n        raise\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef _add_column_if_missing(conn: sqlite3.Connection, table: str, column: str,\n                           definition: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never alters a table that already exists, so\n    a column added to SCHEMA later is added here for databases made before it.\"\"\"\n    existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n    if column not in existing:\n        try:\n            conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n        except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:\n            # Another process started at the same moment and added it first.\n            if \"duplicate column name\" not in str(exc):\n                raise\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        _add_column_if_missing(conn, \"recap\", \"published_at\", \"TEXT\")\n=== app/policy.py\n\"\"\"The permission policy: can this Account do this action to this object?\n\nEvery route asks `can` (through `security.require`); routes never check roles\nthemselves. Unknown actions are denied. Add an action here when a ticket adds a\ncapability. Rules that depend on the object (an Editor's own Draft) take the\n`obj` argument.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nADMIN = \"admin\"\nEDITOR = \"editor\"\n\n# action -> roles allowed to do it\nROLE_RULES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {\n    \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n    \"trips.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n    \"recaps.create\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"recaps.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"recaps.edit\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"recaps.delete\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"recaps.submit\": frozenset({EDITOR}),\n    \"recaps.publish\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n    \"recaps.unpublish\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n    \"recaps.send_back\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n}\n\n# Actions on one Recap. An Editor may do these only to a Draft they Own; an\n# Admin may do them to any Recap. `obj` is the Recap row.\nRECAP_ACTIONS = frozenset({\"recaps.view\", \"recaps.edit\", \"recaps.delete\"})\n\n\n# Only the Editor who Owns a Draft Submits it (an Admin has no row for this).\nOWN_DRAFT_ACTIONS = frozenset({\"recaps.submit\"})\n\n\ndef can(account: Account | None, action: str, obj: object | None = None) -> bool:\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        return False\n    if account.role not in ROLE_RULES.get(action, frozenset()):\n        return False\n    if action in OWN_DRAFT_ACTIONS:\n        return (obj is not None and obj[\"owner_id\"] == account.id\n                and obj[\"status\"] == \"draft\")\n    if action in RECAP_ACTIONS and account.role != ADMIN:\n        return (obj is not None and obj[\"owner_id\"] == account.id\n                and obj[\"status\"] == \"draft\")\n    return True\n=== app/security.py\n\"\"\"Sessions, CSRF and the route guard.\n\nThe session is a signed cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware, itsdangerous\nunderneath) holding the Account id and a CSRF token. The Account itself is\nreread from the database on every request.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import accounts, policy\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nSAFE_METHODS = {\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"OPTIONS\"}\nLOGIN_URL = \"/login\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\nasync def csrf_protect(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"App-wide dependency: refuse any state-changing request without the token.\"\"\"\n    if request.method in SAFE_METHODS:\n        return\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not (isinstance(sent, str) and expected\n            and secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected)):\n        raise HTTPException(403, \"Missing or invalid CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account | None:\n    \"\"\"Reread the signed-in Account; a Deactivated one counts as signed out.\"\"\"\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = accounts.get(account_id) if account_id else None\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.pop(\"account_id\", None)\n        return None\n    return account\n\n\ndef require(action: str) -> Callable[..., Account]:\n    \"\"\"Route dependency: logged out -> login page, not allowed -> 403.\"\"\"\n\n    def guard(account: Account | None = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n        if account is None:\n            raise HTTPException(303, headers={\"Location\": LOGIN_URL})\n        if not policy.can(account, action):\n            raise HTTPException(403, \"You do not have permission to do that\")\n        return account\n\n    return guard\n=== app/slugs.py\n\"\"\"Suggested Slugs. A suggestion is only a starting point; the Admin or Editor\ncan edit it, and uniqueness is checked when the form is saved.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\n\nfrom app.trips import parse_date\n\n\ndef slugify(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"URL-safe form of text: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, joined by\n    single hyphens.\"\"\"\n    ascii_text = (unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKD\", text)\n                  .encode(\"ascii\", \"ignore\").decode())\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", ascii_text.lower()).strip(\"-\")\n\n\ndef is_url_safe(slug: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if slug is what slugify could produce: lowercase ASCII letters and\n    digits joined by single hyphens.\"\"\"\n    return re.fullmatch(r\"[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*\", slug) is not None\n\n\ndef suggest_trip_slug(start_date: str, city: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Start year plus city, such as 2026-chicago; empty until the start date is\n    a real date and the city is known.\"\"\"\n    start, city_slug = parse_date(start_date.strip()), slugify(city)\n    return f\"{start.year}-{city_slug}\" if start and city_slug else \"\"\n=== app/site_state.py\n\"\"\"Site state: the single record of when `cms publish` last rendered the Public\nsite. T08's \"changes not yet live\" notice compares content edit times against it.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app import db\n\n_NOW = \"strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')\"\n\n\ndef record_render() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Stamp now as the time the Public site was last rendered.\"\"\"\n    db.init_db()\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            f\"INSERT INTO site_state (id, last_rendered_at) VALUES (1, {_NOW}) \"\n            f\"ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_rendered_at = {_NOW}\")\n\n\ndef last_rendered() -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"When the Public site was last rendered, or None if it never has.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT last_rendered_at FROM site_state WHERE id = 1\").fetchone()\n    return row[\"last_rendered_at\"] if row else None\n=== app/flash.py\n\"\"\"One-shot notices carried to the next page in the signed session cookie.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\n\nKEY = \"flashes\"\n\n\ndef flash(request: Request, message: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Queue `message` to show on the next page this session renders.\"\"\"\n    request.session[KEY] = [*request.session.get(KEY, []), message]\n\n\ndef take_flashes(request: Request) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The queued notices, removed so each shows once.\"\"\"\n    return request.session.pop(KEY, [])\n=== app/main.py\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin, with /login and /logout beside it; the\npublic site answers at /. Add routes in their own modules under app/routes/ and\ninclude them here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, recaps, trips\nfrom app.security import csrf_protect\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_DEV_DEFAULT:\n        log.warning(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY is not set: sessions are signed with the \"\n                    \"public development key. Development use only.\")\n    db.init_db()\n    # csrf_protect runs on every route, so no state-changing route can skip it.\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", dependencies=[Depends(csrf_protect)])\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"lax\",\n                       https_only=False)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(trips.router)\n    app.include_router(recaps.router)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"site_title\": settings.SITE_TITLE,\n             \"items\": [], \"css_path\": \"style.css\", \"home_path\": \"index.html\",\n             \"instagram_url\": settings.INSTAGRAM_URL},\n        )\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app/markdown.py\n\"\"\"Body -> sanitized HTML. The only place a Body is turned into HTML.\n\nPreview and `cms publish` both call `render_body`, so what the editor shows is\nwhat readers get. markdown-it-py renders first, then nh3 enforces an allowlist.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import Collection\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\nfrom markdown_it.token import Token\n\nALLOWED_TAGS = {\"a\", \"blockquote\", \"br\", \"code\", \"em\", \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\",\n                \"h5\", \"h6\", \"hr\", \"img\", \"li\", \"ol\", \"p\", \"pre\", \"strong\", \"ul\"}\nALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {\"a\": {\"href\"}, \"img\": {\"src\", \"alt\"}}\n\n# markdown-it must parse raw HTML as HTML to tell it from text (with html=False\n# it becomes escaped text instead). It is parsed only to be thrown away: every\n# raw-HTML token is dropped before rendering, so none is ever rendered and none\n# leaves text behind. nh3 below is the second layer, enforcing the allowlist on\n# whatever markdown-it produced.\n_markdown = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\", {\"html\": True})\n\n_RAW_CONTENT_TAG = re.compile(r\"<(/?)(script|style)\\b\", re.I)\n_SCHEME = re.compile(r\"^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.\\-]*:\")\n# nh3 leaves a bare <a> where it dropped the href, and an <img> with no src.\n_BARE_LINK = re.compile(r\"<a>(.*?)</a>\", re.S)\n_SRCLESS_IMG = re.compile(r\"<img(?![^>]*\\bsrc=)[^>]*>\")\n\n\ndef is_relative(target: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True for a path like ``../other/`` or ``images/a.jpg``. Anything with a\n    scheme (http:, mailto:, javascript:), a host (//x) or a root (/x) is not.\"\"\"\n    target = re.sub(r\"[\\x00-\\x20]\", \"\", target).replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\n    return bool(target) and not _SCHEME.match(target) \\\n        and not target.startswith(\"/\")\n\n\ndef _drop_inline_html(children: list[Token]) -> list[Token]:\n    \"\"\"`children` without raw inline tags, and without anything between an\n    opening and closing <script> or <style> (their text is code, not prose).\"\"\"\n    kept, inside = [], None\n    for child in children:\n        if child.type == \"html_inline\":\n            found = _RAW_CONTENT_TAG.match(child.content)\n            if inside and found and found.group(1) and found.group(2).lower() == inside:\n                inside = None\n            elif not inside and found and not found.group(1):\n                inside = found.group(2).lower()\n        elif not inside:\n            kept.append(child)\n    return kept\n\n\ndef _render_without_raw_html(body: str) -> str:\n    tokens = [t for t in _markdown.parse(body) if t.type != \"html_block\"]\n    for token in tokens:\n        if token.type == \"inline\" and token.children:\n            token.children = _drop_inline_html(token.children)\n    return _markdown.renderer.render(tokens, _markdown.options, {})\n\n\ndef render_body(body: str, image_urls: Collection[str] = ()) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The sanitized HTML for a Markdown Body.\n\n    Links survive only if relative. Images survive only if their source is one\n    of `image_urls` (the Recap's own uploaded Images, as `images/<file>`). A removed\n    link keeps its text; a removed image leaves nothing. Raw HTML in the Body is\n    removed whole: a raw block disappears, a raw inline tag disappears and the\n    Markdown text around it stays.\n    \"\"\"\n    own = set(image_urls)\n\n    def keep(tag: str, attr: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n        if tag == \"a\" and attr == \"href\":\n            return value if is_relative(value) else None\n        if tag == \"img\" and attr == \"src\":\n            return value if value in own else None\n        return value\n\n    html = nh3.clean(_render_without_raw_html(body), tags=ALLOWED_TAGS,\n                     attributes=ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES, url_schemes=set(),\n                     link_rel=None, attribute_filter=keep)\n    return _SRCLESS_IMG.sub(\"\", _BARE_LINK.sub(r\"\\1\", html))\n\n\n_IMG_TAG = re.compile(r\"<img\\b[^>]*>\")\n_ALT = re.compile(r'\\balt=\"([^\"]*)\"')\n\n\ndef images_without_alt(body: str, image_urls: Collection[str] = ()) -> int:\n    \"\"\"How many of the Body's kept images have blank alt text. Counted on the\n    output of `render_body`, so only images that would be shown count.\"\"\"\n    return sum(1 for tag in _IMG_TAG.findall(render_body(body, image_urls))\n               if not (m := _ALT.search(tag)) or not m.group(1).strip())\n=== app/publish.py\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import db, images, settings\nfrom app.markdown import images_without_alt, render_body\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\nclass PublishRefused(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The Public site cannot be rendered; the message says which Recap and why.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef _published_recaps() -> dict[int, list]:\n    \"\"\"Published Recaps by trip id, each list in the order they were Published.\n    The only place `cms publish` reads Recaps: nothing else is ever selected.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        rows = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM recap WHERE status = 'published' \"\n            \"ORDER BY published_at, id\").fetchall()\n    by_trip: dict[int, list] = {}\n    for row in rows:\n        by_trip.setdefault(row[\"trip_id\"], []).append(row)\n    return by_trip\n\n\ndef _check_publishable(published: dict[int, list]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse, naming the Recap, before `site/` is touched: an Image with no alt\n    text in a Published Body (it can be edited after Publish), or an Image whose\n    uploaded file is gone. Raises PublishRefused.\"\"\"\n    for recaps in published.values():\n        for recap in recaps:\n            recap_images = images.list_images(recap[\"id\"])\n            if images_without_alt(recap[\"body\"], {\n                    f\"images/{i['filename']}\" for i in recap_images}):\n                raise PublishRefused(\n                    f\"Recap '{recap['slug']}' ({recap['title']}) has an image \"\n                    \"without alt text. Add alt text, then publish again.\")\n            for image in recap_images:\n                if not (settings.UPLOADS / image[\"filename\"]).is_file():\n                    raise PublishRefused(\n                        f\"Recap '{recap['slug']}' ({recap['title']}) uses the \"\n                        f\"image {image['filename']}, whose file is missing \"\n                        f\"from {settings.UPLOADS}.\")\n\n\ndef _write(env: Environment, path: Path, template: str, depth: int,\n           **context) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Render `template` to `path`, with every link back to the site root\n    computed from the page's `depth` below it.\"\"\"\n    root = \"../\" * depth\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    path.write_text(env.get_template(template).render(\n        site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE, css_path=f\"{root}style.css\",\n        home_path=f\"{root}index.html\", instagram_url=settings.INSTAGRAM_URL,\n        **context))\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    published = _published_recaps()\n    _check_publishable(published)\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        trips = [t for t in conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM trip ORDER BY start_date DESC, id DESC\")\n            if t[\"id\"] in published]\n\n    _write(env, out / \"index.html\", \"public/home.html\", 0,\n           title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n           items=[{\"href\": f\"trips/{t['slug']}/\", \"title\": t[\"conference\"],\n                   \"dates\": f\"{t['city']}, {t['start_date']}\"} for t in trips])\n    for trip in trips:\n        trip_dir = out / \"trips\" / trip[\"slug\"]\n        _write(env, trip_dir / \"index.html\", \"public/trip.html\", 2,\n               title=trip[\"conference\"], trip=trip,\n               recaps=published[trip[\"id\"]])\n        for recap in published[trip[\"id\"]]:\n            page_dir = trip_dir / recap[\"slug\"]\n            recap_images = images.list_images(recap[\"id\"])\n            _write(env, page_dir / \"index.html\",\n                   \"public/recap.html\", 3, title=recap[\"title\"], trip=trip,\n                   recap=recap, body_html=render_body(\n                       recap[\"body\"], {f\"images/{i['filename']}\"\n                                       for i in recap_images}))\n            for image in recap_images:\n                (page_dir / \"images\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n                shutil.copy2(settings.UPLOADS / image[\"filename\"],\n                             page_dir / \"images\" / image[\"filename\"])\n    return out\n=== {"parentUuid":"7354b5b6-1afb-4465-a0a0-0feb3f98ea76","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49744d0f-faa0-4995-b293-4e614a407edc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UCceqo5GkjQAEX6fhwoKdf","type":"tool_result","content":"**Permission policy.** A single module answers \"can this Account do this action to this object\". Every route asks it, so there are no ad-hoc role checks scattered across routes. Being logged out redirects to login. Being logged in but not allowed returns 403. The policy rereads the Account on every request, so a Deactivation or role change takes effect at once.\n\n**Login and sessions.** Login takes an email and password at `/login`, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. Sessions use a signed cookie through the existing `itsdangerous` dependency. Sign out clears the session. Login failures show one generic message.\n\n**CSRF.** Each session has a token, rendered as a hidden field in every form that changes state. Any state-changing request without a matching token gets a 403. No new dependency.\n\n**Markdown rendering.** One function turns a Body into HTML: `markdown-it-py`, then `nh3` with an allowlist of formatting tags. It removes:\n- any link whose target is not relative,\n- any image whose source is not one of the Recap's own uploaded Images,\n- all raw HTML.\n\nPreview and `cms publish` both use this same function, so what Preview shows is what readers get.\n\n**Images.** Accepted types are JPEG, PNG, and WebP, checked by file content and not by extension, up to about 5 MB. Images are stored in an uploads folder that is gitignored and outside `site/`. The snippet the console offers is a relative `images/<file>` reference. `cms publish` copies a Published Recap's Images next to its page, so that relative reference resolves.\n\n**Admin console screens.**\n- Login.\n- Dashboard, with counts and the \"changes not yet live\" notice.\n- Recaps list with filters for status, Trip, and Owner (Owner for Admins only), Submitted first for Admins.\n- Recap editor with Preview, Image upload, and action buttons for the transitions above.\n- Trips list and editor.\n- Pages list (filter by status) and editor with Preview and nav position.\n- Accounts list and editor.\n\nAll console routes sit under `/admin`, except `/login` and `/logout`. Screens are server-rendered with Jinja. There is no JavaScript framework and no live preview (ADR-002).\n\n**Admin-only routes.** These must refuse Editors:\n- Trip create, edit, and delete.\n- All Page routes.\n- All Account routes.\n- Publish, Unpublish, and Send back.\n- Editing, Submitting, or deleting a Recap the Editor doesn't Own.\n\n**Public site rendering.** `render_site` writes:\n- the home page (Trips with a Published Recap, newest start date first),\n- one page per such Trip,\n- one page per Published Recap,\n- one page per Published Page,\n- the stylesheet,\n- copied Images.\n\nAddresses take the forms `trips/<trip>/`, `trips/<trip>/<recap>/` and `<page>/`, each as an index file. Every link is computed relative to the page's depth. The Navigation bar is Home followed by the Published Pages by nav position. The footer holds the Instagram link, taken from a constant committed in the repository's settings (not an environment variable), so `cms publish` produces the same footer on any machine with no setup. Its value is the placeholder `https://www.instagram.com/REPLACE-ME/` for now. Nothing that isn't Published is ever read by the renderer.\n\n**Deploy and Backup run from the terminal only.** Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`, both of which already exist. The console has no Deploy or Backup button. \"Only Admins Deploy and Backup\" holds because the terminal belongs to the President.\n\n**`cms backup`.** A new subcommand on the existing CLI. It takes the SQLite online-backup copy of the database and the uploads folder, and zips them with the standard library into `cms-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.zip` in an output folder given as an argument. It refuses any output folder inside the repository. Backup archives are also gitignored as a second safeguard.\n\n**Seed data.** Extend the existing seed script. Its Admin and Editor emails match the test fixture, and passwords come from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. It creates demo content in every status.\n\n**`CONTEXT.md`.** The Deploy entry now says that a Deploy is `cms publish` (render) plus `cms deploy` (push). It is corrected in the same commit that references this spec.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test drives the system from outside and checks what a user or reader would see: HTTP status codes, redirects, page text, and files written to `site/`. Tests don't reach into tables or private functions. They use only the seams that already exist, and no new seams are added.\n\n**Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Tests use `TestClient` with the `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. The fixtures may be extended so each test gets a temporary database with the demo Accounts seeded. That changes how the fixtures are set up, not which seam the tests use. The required tests are:\n\n- **Anonymous visitors**: requesting every console route redirects to login.\n- **Editors on Admin-only routes**: a table-driven test hits every Admin-only route and action listed above as an Editor and expects a 403 or a redirect for each one.\n- **Editors cannot Publish**: an Editor's Publish and Unpublish requests are refused, and the Recap's status stays the same.\n- **Editors cannot touch another person's Recap**: edit, Submit, and delete requests on someone else's Recap are refused, and the Recap is unchanged.\n- **Editors are locked out after Submit**: an Editor can't edit their own Recap once it is Submitted or Published.\n- **Passwords**: the stored password is an argon2 hash and never the plain text. Logging in with the right password works, and with a wrong one fails with the generic message. Signing out ends the session.\n- **Deactivation**: a Deactivated Account can't log in, and its existing session stops working. Deactivating or demoting the last active Admin is refused.\n- **Role changes**: after an Admin changes an Account's role, its permissions follow the new role.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form contains a token, and a POST without a valid token gets a 403.\n- **Recap rules**: Submit, Send back, Publish, and Unpublish each move the status as specified. An empty Body is refused. A Slug that clashes within its Trip is refused. Deleting a Trip that has Recaps is refused.\n- **Image rules**: wrong file types, oversized files, and missing alt text are refused. Publish is refused while the Body has an image without alt text.\n- **Dashboard**: the counts match the seeded data, for both an Admin and an Editor.\n- **Content list**: the status, Trip, and Owner filters return the right Recaps. Editors see only their own Recaps.\n- **Preview**: given a Body containing `<script>`, an external link, and an external image, Preview shows sanitized HTML with all three removed.\n\n**Seam 2: `render_site(out)` into `tmp_path`.** These tests follow the prior art in `tests/test_t00.py`. Using a seeded database, they check:\n\n- Draft and Submitted Recaps, Draft Pages, and Trips with no Published Recap are absent from the output.\n- Published content is present.\n- Body sanitization holds in the output.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"a494f796-1eb3-44c2-88e1-6a639fbc72ce","timestamp":"2026-10-24T17:03:49.299Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"**Permission policy.** A single module answers \"can this Account do this action to this object\".
